peer_requirements.declaration: /.well-known/axn-node.json at the peer's domain, conforming to spec v0.1
peer_requirements.custody: independently administered — separate operator, registrar, hosting account, and billing (the LOCKSS test: ten sites under one administrator are one site in disguise)
peer_requirements.verification: peer must hold bytes whose SHA-256 matches the registry hash for every AXN it claims to preserve; spot-checked at listing and at each reconciliation
peer_requirements.listing: open an issue on leesharks000/alexanarch with the peer's node declaration URL; listing is mechanical upon verification

note: Empty by fact, not by design. Listing requirements above govern entry to this registry. Per the corrected custody doctrine (2026-07-18): a peer-registry entry alone does NOT close the archive's custody limitation. Closure requires an independently administered operator holding a declared reconstructible corpus, demonstrating byte matches against full registry hashes on a documented schedule, retaining audit evidence, able to transfer or serve repair copies, and completing a restoration test. Until then the accurate phrase is: architecture for distributed custody.
